summary:
Daejeon stands under South Korea's national legal framework. The city's own documented signal concerns the courts and institutions located here rather than any Daejeon-specific statute.

On 7 October 2021 the Daejeon District Court ordered the cancellation of Staff Sergeant Byun Hee-soo's discharge from the Army, the first known legal case involving a transgender soldier. The court held that the military should have treated her as female following her legal sex change, that loss of genitalia was not valid grounds for dismissal, and that fitness-for-service review must weigh basic rights. The ruling vindicated her posthumous appeal and stands as dated, court-level proof that a Daejeon court delivered a pro-recognition ruling on transgender military status.

Byun Hee-soo was buried at the National Cemetery in Daejeon on 24 June 2024, the first transgender soldier in South Korea to receive a state burial. Some 60 activists protested at the burial, arguing that the ceremony was marred by discriminatory treatment. She died by suicide in 2021 following her forced 2020 discharge, during which gender dysphoria was classified as a mental disorder and a post-surgery physical-disability finding was recorded, alongside the court appeals. The state burial in Daejeon amounts to official honouring while the institutional stance on transgender service members remains conservative.
tangentialFactors:
The Daejeon District Court's 2021 ruling sits within a national pattern in which military authorities classified the effects of gender-affirming surgery as a handicap, while courts pushed back on that classification at trial level.

The state burial at Daejeon National Cemetery in June 2024 proceeded alongside activist objections to discriminatory treatment, indicating that official honour and contested practice coexist rather than one replacing the other.
localsOnly:
Residents of Daejeon can point to a local court whose 2021 judgment in the Byun Hee-soo case established that a soldier's legal sex change must be respected in fitness review and that genital loss is not a valid ground for dismissal.

Daejeon National Cemetery, where Byun Hee-soo was interred on 24 June 2024, is the site of the state's recognition of her service; the burial drew roughly 60 protesters who contested how it was conducted.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the Daejeon District Court's 2021 reasoning has been applied in subsequent military fitness reviews elsewhere is not sourced here.

The specific grounds on which activists said the June 2024 burial was discriminatory are described only in general terms in the available material and remain unresolved.

No Daejeon-specific data on restroom access, healthcare access, hate-crime incidence, or anti-discrimination protection was identified in this inventory; those layers are carried by the national record.
